conventions.convention: Population values are fixed. Nonempty strata receive independent SRSWOR samples with integer sizes 1 ≤ n_h ≤ N_h; the joint design law is the product of the uniform within-stratum laws.
For noncertainty strata, S_h² uses denominator N_h−1 and S_h is its nonnegative square root. Certainty strata contribute their fixed totals and require no variance term, including singleton strata.

Neyman allocation optimizes an uncapped continuous expression over a nonempty set J with S_h > 0, x_h > 0 and sum x_h = n★ > 0, holding other allocations fixed. Integer, capacity and minimum-sample constraints are excluded.
Cost allocation uses positive per-unit costs and the equality budget sum c_h x_h = C★ > 0 over positive real allocations; fixed-stratum costs have already been removed from the residual budget.

load_bearing.statement: A finite population is partitioned into nonempty strata, sampled independently by SRSWOR with 1 ≤ n_h ≤ N_h. The stratified total estimator is sum_h N_h times the sample mean in stratum h.
Under the stratified SRSWOR design, E_d[T̂_st] = sum_i y_i and Var_d(T̂_st) = sum_{h:n_h<N_h} N_h²(1−n_h/N_h)S_h²/n_h. Certainty strata contribute zero and require no within-stratum variance term.

For a nonempty set J of variable noncertainty strata with S_h > 0, holding other allocations fixed, the uncapped continuous variance expression on x_h > 0 and sum_{h∈J} x_h = n★ > 0 has the unique minimizer x_h = n★ N_h S_h / sum_{k∈J} N_k S_k.

For a nonempty set J of variable noncertainty strata with S_h > 0, positive costs c_h and residual budget C★ > 0, holding other allocations fixed, the uncapped continuous variance expression on x_h > 0 and sum_{h∈J} c_h x_h = C★ has the unique minimizer x_h = C★(N_h S_h/√c_h) / sum_{k∈J} N_k S_k √c_k.

seams_checked.note: The supplier fixes population values and randomizes sampled subsets. The consumer's product law is a normalized finite design; its inclusion probabilities n_h/N_h are positive, and its estimator equals the observed-record HT total. The HT unbiasedness statement is used with its required positive inclusion probabilities.

The consumer uses the supplier's uniform n-element-subset design and SRSWOR mean variance with denominator N_h−1. Every noncertainty stratum has N_h > 1, including when n_h = 1. Certainty strata, including singletons, are handled directly as constants. No pair-inclusion positivity assumption is imported from the separate variance-estimator result.
